'''Ralph Martin Kaufmann''' (born August 4, 1969) is a German-American mathematician working in the United States.

== Career ==
Kaufmann studied mathematics, physics and philosophy at the [[University of Bonn]]. He obtained a master's degree in Physics in 1994 under the supervision of [[Werner Nahm]] and a master's degree in philosophy under the supervision of Rainer Stuhlmann-Laeisz in 1996. His doctoral studies were carried out at the [[Max Planck Institute for Mathematics]] under the supervision of [[Yuri Manin]], and he graduated summa cum laude from [[University of Bonn]] in 1997 with a thesis entitled "The geometry of the moduli space of pointed curves, the tensor product in the theory of Frobenius manifolds and the explicit Künneth formula in quantum cohomology".<ref>Bonner Mathematische Schriften 312, 95 p., Bonn 1997.</ref>

He remained at the Max Planck Institute for one year after his graduation as a researcher before moving to the [[Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques]] for a year with a Marie Curie Fellowship from the European Union.

In 1999 Kaufmann moved to the United States, where he has held several positions. He arrived at his current institution, [[Purdue University]], in 2007 as an associate professor, being promoted to full professor in 2012.

Kaufmann has been a member of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in [[Princeton University|Princeton]],<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/ralph-martin-kaufmann|title=Ralph Martin Kaufmann|work=Institute for Advanced Study|access-date=2018-01-03|language=en}}</ref> and has held visiting positions at the [[Max Planck Institute for Mathematics]] in [[Bonn]], the [[Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques]], the [[Mittag-Leffler Institute]] in [[Stockholm]], the [[Isaac Newton Institute]] in [[Cambridge]], the [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]] in [[Berkeley, California]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.math.purdue.edu/~rkaufman/|title=Ralph M. Kaufmann|website=[[Purdue University]], Department of Mathematics|access-date=2018-01-03}}</ref> and the Hamburg Institute for Advanced Study.<ref>[https://hias-hamburg.de/fellow/ralph-kaufmann/ hias-hamburg.de]</ref>

== Research ==

Kaufmann's research has covered different areas of mathematics and theoretical physics. After briefly working on the [[Virasoro algebra]],<ref>Kaufmann, Ralph M.
"Path Space Decompositions for the Virasoro Algebra and its Verma Modules". 
Internat. J. of Modern Phys. A 10 (1995), 943-961.</ref> he started to work on the quantum cohomology of a product<ref>[[Maxim Kontsevich]] and [[Yuri Manin]] with appendix by R. Kaufmann. 
"Quantum cohomology of a product".
Invent. Math. 124 (1996), 313-339.</ref> and the Künneth formula, obtaining results on explicit formulas<ref>Kaufmann, Ralph M.
"The intersection form in H*(M0,n) and the explicit Künneth formula in quantum cohomology".
Internat. Math. Res. Notices 19 (1996), 929-954.</ref> and global results.<ref>Kaufmann, Ralph M.
"The tensor product in the theory of Frobenius manifolds".
Internat. J. of Math. 10 (1999), 159-206</ref> In collaboration with [[Yuri Manin]] and [[Don Zagier]] he started the study of higher Weil–Peterson volumes,<ref>Kaufmann, R.; Manin, Yu.; and Zagier, D. 
"Higher Weil-Petersson Volumes of Moduli Spaces of Stable n-pointed Curves".
Comm. Math. Phys. 181 (1996), 763-787.</ref> later continued by Losef–Manin and [[Maryam Mirzakhani]]. Kaufmann then started to study stringy and mirror phenomena for [[orbifold]]s<ref>Kaufmann, Ralph M.  
"Orbifolding Frobenius Algebras".  
Internat. J. of Math. 14 (2003), 573-619</ref>  and singularities.<ref>Kaufmann, Ralph M.
"Singularities with Symmetries, Orbifold Frobenius algebras and Mirror Symmetry"
Contemp. Math., 403 (2006), 67-116</ref> This led to the invention of stringy K-theory.<ref>Jarvis, T.; Kaufmann, R. and Kimura, T. 
"Stringy K-theory and the Chern character". 
Inventiones Math. 168, 1 (2007), 23-81</ref><ref>
Kaufmann, Ralph M.
"Global Stringy Orbifold Cohomology, K-Theory and de Rham Theory".
Letters in Mathematical Physics, 94, 2 (2010) 165-195.</ref>

Kaufmann has also worked on [[string topology]], invented by Moira Chas and [[Dennis Sullivan]], and [[operad theory]].<ref>
Kaufmann, Ralph M.; Livernet, Muriel and Penner, Robert C.  
"Arc Operads and Arc Algebras". 
Geometry and Topology 7 (2003), 511-568.</ref><ref name="Kaufmann pp. 237–300">{{cite journal | last=Kaufmann | first=Ralph M | title=On several varieties of cacti and their relations | journal=Algebraic & Geometric Topology | publisher=Mathematical Sciences Publishers | volume=5 | issue=1 | date=15 April 2005 | issn=1472-2739 | doi=10.2140/agt.2005.5.237 | pages=237–300| s2cid=2067462 | doi-access=free | arxiv=math/0209131 }}</ref><ref>
Kaufmann, Ralph M.
"On Spineless Cacti, Deligne's Conjecture and Connes-Kreimer's Hopf Algebra."
Topology 46, 1 (2007), 39-88.</ref><ref>
Kaufmann, Ralph M.  
"Operads, Moduli of Surfaces and Quantum Algebras", 
in: N. Tongring and R. C. Penner "Woods Hole Mathematics. Perspectives in Mathematics and Physics",
Series on Knots and Everything - Vol. 34, World Scientific 2004.
</ref><ref>{{cite journal
| first1=Ralph M. | last1=Kaufmann
|first2=Rachel | last2=Schwell
| title=Associahedra, cyclohedra and a topological solution to the <math>A_\infty</math>-Deligne conjecture
| journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]]
| volume=223
| issue=6
| year=2010
| pages=2166–2199
| doi=10.1016/j.aim.2009.11.001 | doi-access=free| hdl=21.11116/0000-0004-23DD-C
| hdl-access=free
| arxiv=0710.3967
}}</ref> Here he first proved a cyclic version of [[Pierre Deligne]]'s conjecture in deformation theory<ref>Kaufmann, Ralph M.
"A proof of a cyclic version of Deligne's conjecture via Cacti"
Math. Res. Letters 15, 5 (2008), 901--921.</ref> and provided an extension of string topology to moduli spaces.<ref>Kaufmann, Ralph M. 
"Moduli space actions on the Hochschild cochain complex I: cell models".
Journal of Noncommutative Geometry 1, 3 (2007) 333-384., Kaufmann, Ralph M. 
"Moduli space actions on the Hochschild cochain complex II: correlators". 
Journal of Noncommutative Geometry 2, 3 (2008), 283-332.</ref><ref>
Kaufmann, Ralph M. 
"Open/Closed String Topology and Moduli Space Actions via Open/Closed Hochschild Actions". 
SIGMA 6 (2010) 036, 33 pages.
 Kaufmann, Ralph M.</ref><ref>
"Graphs, strings and actions"
in: Algebra, Arithmetic and Geometry Volume II: In Honor of Yu. I. Manin. 
Progress in Mathematics 270, 127--178. Birhauser, Boston (2010).</ref><ref>Kaufmann, Ralph M.
"Arc Geometry and Algebra: Foliations, Moduli Spaces, String Topology and Field Theory".
Chapter in Handbook of Teichmüller Theory IV. 
Ed: Athanase Papadopoulos. European Mathematical Society 2014.</ref>

More recently Kaufmann has introduced the notion of Feynman categories<ref>
Kaufmann, Ralph M. and Ward, Benjamin C.
"Feynman categories".
Astérisque 387 (2017), x+161 pages.
</ref> to give a common framework for various aspects of algebra, geometry, topology, and category theory.<ref>Kaufmann, Ralph M., Ward, Benjamin C. and Zuniga, J. Javier 
"The odd origin of Gerstenhaber brackets, Batalin-Vilkovisky operators and the master equations".
Journal of Math. Phys. 56 (2015), 103504.</ref><ref>Kaufmann, Ralph M., Lucas, Jason.
"Decorated Feynman categories". 
arXiv:1602.00823
J. of Noncommutative Geometry to appear.</ref><ref>Berger, Clemens and Kaufmann, Ralph M. 
"Comprehensive Factorization Systems". 
arXiv:1710.09438. Special Issue of Tbilisi Mathematical Journal in honor of Peter J. Freyd and F.W. Lawvere on the occasion of their 80th birthdays to appear</ref>

In mathematical physics, he has also studied the geometry of wire networks<ref>Kaufmann, Ralph M., Khlebnikov, Sergei and Wehefritz-Kaufmann, Birgit.
"The geometry of the Double Gyroid wire network: Quantum and Classical".
  Journal of Noncommutative Geometry, 6 (2012), 623-664.</ref> as well as periodic systems<ref>Kaufmann, 
Ralph M., Khlebnikov, Sergei and Wehefritz-Kaufmann, Birgit. 
"Singularities, swallowtails and Dirac points. An analysis for families of Hamiltonians 
and applications to wire networks, especially the Gyroid".
Annals of Physics, 327 (2012), 2865-2884.</ref><ref>Kaufmann, Ralph M., Khlebnikov, Sergei and Wehefritz-Kaufmann, Birgit.
"Re-gauging groupoid, symmetries and degeneracies for Graph Hamiltonians and applications to the Gyroid wire network".
Ann. H. Poincaré  7, 6 (2016),  1383-1414.</ref> and topological insulators.<ref>Kaufmann, Ralph M., Li, Dan, and Wehefritz-Kaufmann, Birgit.
"Notes on topological insulators".
Reviews in Math. Physics, Vol. 28, No. 10 (2016) 1630003</ref>

In philosophy, he has recently worked on [[Hegel]]'s theory of mathematics<ref>
Kaufmann, Ralph M. and Yeomans, Christopher L.
"Math by Pure Thinking: R First and the Divergence Of Measures in Hegel's Philosophy of Mathematics".
European Journal of Philosophy, ahead of print.</ref><ref>
Kaufmann, Ralph M. and Yeomans, Christopher L. 
"Hegel on Calculus". History of Philosophy Quarterly, to appear.
</ref> and on [[Friedrich Hölderlin]].<ref>
Kaufmann, Ralph M. Der Dichter spricht: Eine Rezeption Hölderlins 'Verfahrensweise des Poetischen Geistes'",
Zeitschrift für Kulturphilosophie, 2017/1  "Sprache und Gestalt", Meiner Verlag, Hamburg.</ref>
